english.title: Procure a broadcast from a ship / aircraft while it is in / over the UK / external waters
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) procured a broadcast to be made from

(A)_[a ship]_
(B)_[an aircraft]_

while it was

(C)_[in]_
(D)_[over]_

(E)_[the United Kingdom]_
(F)_[external waters]_
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 77(1)(a) and (4) and 93(1) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 93(3) of the Wireless Telegraphy Act 2006 provides that proceedings in England and Wales for this offence may be brought only by OFCOM or by or with the consent of the Secretary of State or the DPP.
(ii) Section 110 of the Act provides for criminal liability of company directors, managers, etc.
(iii) Section 94 of the Act provides a saving for broadcasts made under and in accordance with a wireless telegraphy licence.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022, see paragraph 16 of Schedule 8 to the Act; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see section 35(2)(a) of the Act and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
